name: The Warden Marches
people: Argonian garrisons of the Archwardens' frontier screen and the ex-Archein families who keep the old Imperial forts; the Blackguards' heirs at the Rose
about: The stone forts, keeps and posts the Empire built are the only dry, walled ground in much of the marsh, and in 4E 201 they are held by Argonians, not Imperials. Small garrisons of the Archwardens (the An-Xileel successor administration) man the '-moth' forts as toll stations, river watches and the screen facing Morrowind; the families who staff them are mostly old Archein lines who changed their letterhead after the secession, so their manners, ranks and paperwork are still half Cyrodiilic. Thorn and its camps, mine and outposts belong to the same world: saltrice fields and timber held by ex-Archein field-owners and freed labourers' descendants under Vicecanons. The forts have no Hist, so their people go home to a village tree to hatch and bury. Blackrose Prison is the exception: the Rose is held by the prison-born Blackguards' heirs under a Naga raj-kaal, who run it as their own and resent the word prison.
why: Every crimson place is an Imperial foundation: the '-moth' forts follow the Legion's naming (Fort Swampmoth in Black Marsh, Fort Moonmoth and Fort Frostmoth elsewhere), Blackrose Prison is the canon Imperial prison (Lore:Blackrose Prison), and Thorn is the Dres slave-raid city with Imperial and Archein ties (Lore:Thorn). Canon records no Imperial presence after 4E 48 (topics/foreign-powers.md), so the forts cannot be Legion in 4E 201. The owner's rulings settle the rest: Fort Swampmoth is held, but not by the Empire (extrapolation/owner-questions.md); the successor state keeps a frontier screen and customs (argonia-4e201-state.md §1); Archein families survive performing the same tolls and levies in the state's name (§2); Thorn is run by Vicecanons and field-owners (§Thorn); the Rose is reoccupied by the Blackguards' heirs (owner Q3, Lore:Blackrose Prison). Imperial forts carry no Hist (topics/hist-placement.md). UESP has no page for Fort Gysilla, Chalkmoth, Reedmoth, Shellmoth, Silvermoth, Thornmoth, Willowmoth, Southwatch Keep, Bell Station or Aphon Belvedere (searched 2026-11-08): Project Tamriel names. The one-culture reading (forts plus Thorn) is EXTRAPOLATED.

name: The Root-Folk of Helstrom
people: Saxhleel of the Middle Argonian Hist forest, under Helstrom's trees
about: The heartland people of the great Hist forest, the most traditional Argonians in the province. They build nothing in stone, live on stilts and in root-hollows, and move by water; their small outposts are hunting, sap-gathering and egg-tending stations spread through Murkwood and the Lake Ulaish country. Helstrom, never taken by any invader, is their centre and the great Root Talk convocation, the occasional gathering at which the Hist speak to all the tribes, is held there. They accept the Archwardens' seat at Helstrom as a fact and do not obey it. They say the trees decide what matters. Outsiders who come uninvited into the interior do not come back.
why: Helstrom is the canon heartland city, 'the immortal capital of the Argonians', in Middle Argonia where the Hist grow (Lore:Helstrom, story/lore/helstrom.md, regions/middle-argonia.md). The owner ruled the Root Talk convocation at Helstrom (Q2, argonia-4e201-state.md) and the state doc places the successor seat there. The cluster's 17 unnamed outposts lie through Murkwood, Lake Ulaish and the Arnesian jungle, the inner swamp; Guxal and Yuva-Goli have no UESP page. Canon gives no tribe name for Helstrom's people, so the name is ours.

name: The Archon Harbour Folk
people: Amphibious Argonians of Archon and its pilots, wharfingers and ferrymen
about: A port people who work the water in three dimensions: children play underwater games, guar are kept that breathe underwater, and cargo is moved as often under the surface as over it. Archon is the province's principal legal port, run by a harbour authority and merchant council in the East Empire Company's old buildings, with the state's customs officers alongside. A charter separates licensed trade from piracy. The town charters the pirates that it cannot defeat. Its ferrymen run the inland crossings that feed the old Archon, Lilmoth, Soulrest and Tear trade line, Lujei Ferry among them. Archon was barely touched by 4E 48 and is the most at ease of the cities with the successor state, but it pays the state as little as it can.
why: Archon is canon (Lore:Archon; story/lore/archon.md): eastern port, EEC stop, letters of marque in 1E 2833, Shadowscale school closed 4E 187. Its 4E 201 state (harbour authority, charter tradition, amphibious civic life) is argonia-4e201-state.md §Archon. Lujei Ferry, far to the west by Blackrose, shares Archon's square; the reading that a ferry is a harbour-folk post on the trade line is ours (reasoning: a ferry is a trade work, and Archon is where the province's legal trade is organised). Lujei Ferry has no UESP page.

name: The Naka-Desh (Riverbacks)
people: Naka-Desh Argonians of the Blackwood and Kotherra rivers
about: Wide-faced, large-eyed Argonians with broad webs on forearms and throat, who see no reason to travel beyond their Hist's roots. They fish the black rivers south and east of Gideon with osheeja gars and keep small river stations and no towns. They are taken for secretive but are simply incurious, with one exception: they love riddles, and a stranger who trades a good one is let pass. They were close friends of the Kothringi and still hang chimes in their memory. They ignore the Archwardens, deal with Gideon only for salt and iron, and are rumoured to be the Blackwood tribe that says Gideon's Hist cutting was taken from them.
why: The Naka-Desh are canon, a morphologically distinct breed of Blackwood (Lore:Argonian; tribes.md), friends of the Kothringi (lost-peoples.md). Indigo's five outposts lie in Nha-Enasa, Kotherra Mangroves, Banujha Basin and Cape Percar, the river country around Gideon's Blackwood, and are outposts only, which fits a people who will not build beyond their tree. hist-placement.md names a Gloommire tribe claiming Gideon's cutting. Placing the Naka-Desh on this cluster is our reading.

name: The Sedge-Wardens of Jal-Veesa (Veesa-Teeleel)
people: Northern Argonians of the Valley of Storms and Barsaebica
about: A reed-cutting, weir-building people of the northern valleys between Stormhold and the Barsaebic ruins. They keep the sedge beds and fish weirs that feed Stormhold, and they guard the Ayleid ruins in their country, which they hold to be sick ground, against looters. Jal-Veesa, their one town, is a market of reed boats, mats and dried fish beside a Hist pool. They trade daily with Stormhold's Dunmer and Argonians and send men to the frontier screen for pay, but keep their own elders and refuse the Vicecanons' courts. They remember the Dunmer slave-raids along this border and are courteous to Dunmer without trusting them.
why: Jal-Veesa and its five outposts lie in the Valley of Storms, Chixathe Mesa and Barsaebica, the Shadowfen border country north and west of Stormhold (Lore:Stormhold; story/lore/stormhold.md; key.json: Barsaebic Ayleid ruins in the north-west). UESP has no page for Jal-Veesa. Canon gives no tribe here, so the tribe, its name (in the -leel style of Kota-Vimleel and Gee-Rusleel, tribes.md) and its ways are AGENT_INVENTED; its border trade and memory of Dunmer slaving follow from Stormhold's canon history.

name: The Agaceph
about: Needle-faced Argonians whose scales come in a rainbow of ruby, lemon, green, purple, blue and orange. They travel on razor-thin one-person rafts driven by the tail, live in small hamlets on the eastern Okuwun-Rahei waters, and are educated after their fashion: they read, keep books taken from dead missions, and are accomplished illusionists, as most day labourers in Black Marsh are. Yulca is their one town. They are wary of strangers and will freeze an intruder with a spell before deciding what to do with him. They have no use for the Archwardens and little for the cities.
why: The Agaceph are canon, exclusive to Middle Argonia (Lore:Argonian via tribes.md and regions/middle-argonia.md), and are the only canon interior breed that is not a camp people: the map key already gives the Paatru and Sarpa their own camps (key.json). Lime's hamlets and town lie in Okuwun-Rahei and Chixathe Mesa, on the eastern side of Middle Argonia. Yulca, Hirecan, Icalca, Xibcan and Yina have no UESP page. The placement is ours.

name: The Hutan-Tzel
people: The Hutan-Tzel tribe of the Panther River, north-west of Helstrom
about: A tribe of the upper Panther River and the Murkwood edge, governed by an elder styled naheesh. They mark their ground with totems carved in runes only they can read; meddling with one draws dangerous beasts. They keep no towns, only fortified outposts along the river, and are cautiously willing to bargain with outsiders who come openly. They sit between Helstrom's Root-Folk and the Gideon country and are often go-betweens for both.
why: The Hutan-Tzel are canon: their own tribe on the Panther River north-west of Helstrom, with an elder Naheesh Nurwul and rune totems (Online, via tribes.md and regions/middle-argonia.md, Hutan-Tzel/Rockguard). Magenta's four outposts lie in Murkwood and Blackwood west and north-west of Helstrom, in that country. Their survival from 2E to 4E 201 and this placement are ours.

name: The Island of Blackrose
people: Argonians and the mixed descendants of prison staff, ex-prisoners, deserters and refugees of Blackrose and its lake villages
about: A lake-island city and its ring of stilt villages at the meeting of three rivers, the hinge of the south through which everything moving between Murkwood, Oliis Bay and Bramman's river passes. The city is governed by whoever holds the island core. The government is narrow, defensive and self-perpetuating and it claims legitimacy by possession. The villages around the lake pay it for protection and toll their own channels. The city's Hist is drowned in the lake and reached only by boat and dive, so the island core controls hatching and naming. Its people are the oddest mix in the province and trust no institution; the Rose, a day's march off and not theirs, is their standing problem.
why: Blackrose is canon (Lore:Blackrose; story/lore/blackrose.md). Its 4E 201 state, the drowned Hist and the Rose's separation are owner rulings and argonia-4e201-state.md §Blackrose. All five olive places lie in the Tulmek Washes around the city; Amalaja, Ka-Asei, Lujei and Natai have no UESP page.

name: The Chime-Keepers (Kothringi-named towns)
people: Argonians who resettled the Kothringi towns of the interior after 2E 560, with a few mixed families
about: When the Knahaten Flu killed the Kothringi in 2E 560, Argonians, immune, moved into their empty towns between Helstrom and Blackrose and kept the old names, Korydon, Toklea, Tydeos and the rest, because a name belonged to the place. Over the centuries they took on Kothringi ways the Hist did not forbid: stone footings under stilt houses, chimes of tin and copper hung from every eave, metal-woven rope, shallow-draft sail-and-paddle boats and a quiet regard for Z'en and Dibella beside Sithis. They are craftsmen and traders, better off than their neighbours, and their towns are the most orderly in the interior. The nativists of 4E 48 called them half-foreign, and they do not forget it; they deal with the Archwardens coldly and with Gideon warmly.
why: Canon says the Kothringi died out in 2E 560 (Lore:Kothringi; lost-peoples.md), and a surviving Kothringi community in 4E 201 is not defensible (lost-peoples.md), so the towns cannot be Kothringi-held. Canon places 'the vast complicated ruins of the Kothringi capitals' in the deep interior and Kothringi in the Blackrose region (lost-peoples.md, The Argonian Account Bk 4), and attests friendship and cultural exchange between Kothringi and Argonians (the Naka-Desh loved their music) and Gideon's Dibella devotion inherited from the Kothringi substrate (gideon.md). The oxblood towns lie in Ultherus Swamp, Aunike Ridge, Murkwood, Banujha and the Tulmek Washes, between Helstrom and Blackrose, and the key puts Kothringi stone ruins nearby. Reading: Argonian resettlers keeping Kothringi names. UESP has no page for Korydon, Toklea or the hamlets. The people and their name are AGENT_INVENTED on that canon base.

name: The Gideon Frontier
people: Lukiul Argonians and Nibenese-descended families of Gideon and the Blackwood border
about: The most Cyrodiilic country in Argonia: majority lukiul Argonians, assimilated to Imperial habits, beside Nibenese families two centuries settled. Gideon keeps written records, a working courthouse and a civic council in the old Governor's Mansion; its villages trade along the Blackwood Road to Leyawiin when the monsoon allows, hunt, deal in herbs and red-clay pottery. Dibella is worshipped here, a devotion the region took from the Kothringi. The An-Xileel's weapon killed Gideon's lukiul majority in 4E 48. The town openly denies the successor state's legitimacy. The ruin of Castle Giovesse and the old customs post at Slough Point belong to this frontier.
why: Gideon is canon (Lore:Gideon; story/lore/gideon.md): lukiul majority, Nibenese families, Dibella, Castle Giovesse, active in the 4E. The 4E 201 politics are argonia-4e201-state.md §Gideon and the owner's Q1. Slough Point is the canon Imperial census-and-excise post on the border (The Argonian Account Bk 1, secondary-settlements.md); Umpholo is the canon interior Temple of Mara of 3E 378 (secondary-settlements.md) but is not in this cluster. Armanias, Olvani, Hixinoag and Gul-Tej have no UESP page; the members lie in Nha-Enasa, Kotherra Mangroves, Barsaebica and Blackwood around Gideon.

name: The Spray-Folk of Seafalls
people: Coastal Argonians of Seafalls, beyond Hist reach
about: A single cliff-and-surf village on the eastern coast north of Archon, under the falls where a river drops to the sea. Its people live too far from any tree to hear the Hist clearly, and like the Tide-Born of Solstice they hold that the sea carries the memories the Hist let fall: they nest on the shoals, leave votives in the spray and keep death-dancers for their burials. Hatching and naming mean a long journey inland, so their numbers stay small. They pilot for Archon's shipping and keep apart from the Archwardens and the tribes alike.
why: Seafalls is named in canon as Archon's neighbour to the north-north-east (story/lore/archon.md) but has no UESP page of its own. It is the only place of its colour. The Izta-Ahuak (Tide-Born) of Solstice are canon's model for Argonians beyond Hist reach (tribes.md; hist-placement.md). Applying that model to Seafalls, and the people's name, are AGENT_INVENTED.

name: The Three Waters Tribe
people: Argonians of the Nushara Bayou between Archon and Lilmoth
about: A bayou people of the waters behind the south-east coast, living in hamlets of reed houses on rafts and stilts and moving them as the channels shift. They net, trap and gather shellfish and rice, and they run the back-water routes between Archon and the Lilmoth delta that the customs officers do not see. Uluo is their one town and the seat of their elder. They have long dealt with Archon as equals and send their own to sit with its merchants. They were untouched by Umbriel and wary of the An-Xileel both before and after it.
why: The Three Waters Tribe is canon: an eastern tribe whose elder Nuetepa was active in Archon in the 2E (tribes.md). Plum's six places lie in the Nushara Bayou and the Althii Archipelago, between Archon and Lilmoth. Uluo, Inoio, Shalaia, Siluo, Tapauo and Xi-Inou have no UESP page. Thornmarsh and Archon were barely touched by 4E 48 (argonia-4e201-state.md §9). The placement and their 4E 201 life are ours.

name: Lilmoth and the Murkmire Coast
people: Argonians of rebuilt Lilmoth, its delta villages and estates, with a foreign dock population
about: A smaller, lower, wholly Argonian town on stilts over the mass grave of 4E 48, rebuilt but not restored, with its Old Imperial quarter left drowned. A merchant council runs it, as it has twice before, and the old rule that unlicensed foreigners stay on the docks is a lapsed law some officials still enforce. Its third Hist is young and feared: a rotating tree-minder's post and a two-tender rule ensure that communion is never held by a single person again. The farms, rice estates, ferries and villages of the delta and the Althii islands feed it and trade through it; Truowa, a city up the Nushara waters, belongs to its trade. Lilmoth was the An-Xileel's seat and their weapon killed it, so it is commercially strong and openly hostile to the successor state.
why: Lilmoth is canon (Lore:Lilmoth; story/lore/lilmoth.md), destroyed in 4E 48; its 4E 201 state is owner ruling Q4 and argonia-4e201-state.md §Lilmoth. The Hereguard rice plantation of the delta is canon (lilmoth.md). The 17 rose places lie in the Althii Archipelago, the Tulmek Washes and the Lilmoth delta. Truowa, Nundi, Oju, Sal-Axan, Tei-Kur and Karketa have no UESP page.

name: The Clay-Mound People of Aroxhu (Oxhu-Teeleel)
people: Argonians of the eastern Okuwun-Rahei mound country
about: The most populous tribal country of the east interior, built on raised mounds of red clay above the flood, with Aroxhu as its great mound-town. They farm the mound slopes, fire pottery and trade clay and dye down the rivers to Archon and Thorn. A council of village elders meets at Aroxhu under its Hist and speaks for the whole confederacy, so the Archwardens must bargain with it. They avoid the Agaceph and the Paatru and fight with them often, without lasting grudges, as Argonian tribes do.
why: The ten rust places (Aroxhu a city, Inoja a town, eight villages) lie mostly in Okuwun-Rahei with outliers in Hatandros Bight, Nushara Bayou, Lake Ulaish and Chixathe Mesa: a large, dense, settled polity in the east of Middle Argonia, where canon puts many unnamed tribes ('scores more exist', Tribes of Murkmire, tribes.md). None of the names has a UESP page. Red clay and pottery are canon trades of the marsh (Gideon's rootworm red clay, Onkobra pottery, argonia-4e201-state.md). Grudges between tribes expire (tribes.md). The tribe, its name and its confederacy are AGENT_INVENTED.

name: The Stone-Sleepers of Tsonac (Tsona-Kaleel)
people: Argonians of the Arnesian jungle uplands north and west of Thorn
about: A jungle people of the uplands between Thorn and Middle Argonia who, unusually for Argonians, still build in stone, over old Velothi and Ayleid foundations in the Arnesian country. Tsonac, their city, is terraced stone and timber around a Hist they say is asleep, and they live by its dreams, as read by a tree-minder. They hunt and quarry, sell stone and timber to Thorn, and fear and despise the old slavers of the forts. They treat the Archwardens as one more power to be outlasted.
why: Tsonac and four hamlets lie in Chixathe Mesa, the Arnesian jungle and Hatandros Bight, north-west of Thorn. Lore:Arnesia names this country as settled by Barsaebic Ayleids and Cantemiric Velothi. Canon's Xit-Xaht were a rare Argonian tribe that never stopped building in stone, under a Hist (Tsono-Xuhil) their neighbours put to sleep (tribes.md); the name Tsonac echoes it. The stone-building, sleeping-Hist reading and the people's name are AGENT_INVENTED; no UESP page exists for Tsonac or the hamlets.

name: The Mine-Burners of the Banujha (Banu-Jaleel)
people: Interior Argonians of the Banujha Basin and Cape Percar hinterland of Soulrest
about: The tribes of the basin behind Soulrest who burned the Imperial mines and timber concessions in 3E 427 and have never been reconciled to the coast. They live in fortified towns, Jarecai and Kharaxos (a name left from older maps that they never bothered to change), and watch posts along the basin's edges. Their Hist is the nearest to Soulrest, so the port's Argonians must come into their country to hatch, name and bury, which gives them a hold over the city that they use. They are one side of Soulrest's struggle for regional hegemony and despise the ex-Imperial administrators on the other side.
why: Six of seven steel-blue places lie in the Banujha Basin, the hinterland of Soulrest (umber). Canon records the tribes of Soulrest's interior destroying its mines and concessions in 3E 427 and an unexplained struggle for regional hegemony there (Lore:Soulrest; story/lore/soulrest.md; argonia-4e201-state.md §Soulrest). The owner ruled Soulrest has no Hist in the city, so its Argonians go inland into those people's country (owner-questions.md). Jarecai and Kharaxos have no UESP page. The people's name and their towns' detail are AGENT_INVENTED.

name: The Shadowfen Border (Stormhold)
people: Argonians and Dunmer of Stormhold and the stone-causeway farmsteads
about: Stormhold's culture is the province's oldest mixed one: Argonians beside the largest and oldest Dunmer minority in Argonia, descended from a colonial population. Its people build stone causeways and farmsteads on raised ground, are governed by Vicecanons, the civil magistrate office the city invented, and hold the river customs and the state's working offices on the Morrowind border. The farms, outposts and hamlets in this style, Surkina, Tenmal and those further south such as Julo, Luntoc and Yalugo, are smallholdings in the Stormhold manner, and a few distant farmsteads and the Seafalls lighthouse follow the same habit of raised stone. Their politics are pragmatic: they have always had to live with outsiders, and the memory of the Dunmer slave trade is local and long.
why: Stormhold is canon (Lore:Stormhold; story/lore/stormhold.md): Shadowfen city, Dunmer slaving foothold, the Vicecanon office, the stone causeway to Bogmother, the Conclave of Baal. Its 4E 201 state is argonia-4e201-state.md §Stormhold. The cluster's core lies in the Valley of Storms and Barsaebica around Stormhold; Julo, Luntoc and Yalugo share its square tint with a slightly different glyph; the four places at cells 28..31,-86..-89 (two farms, a homestead, an outpost and Seafalls Lighthouse) lie on the east coast far from Stormhold, and their membership is read as a building habit, not a polity. Surkina, Tenmal, Julo, Luntoc and Yalugo have no UESP page.

name: Soulrest and the Topal Coast
people: Argonians, Khajiit, Imperial-descended administrators and Bosmer seafarers of Soulrest, Cape Percar and the Topal shore
about: Soulrest was the Third Era capital and is now an administrative city whose Imperial government quarter is half empty. Its people are the most mixed in the province. A merchant council, an ex-Imperial civil apparatus with no sovereign and the river interests contest it, and the mine-burning tribes of the interior hold the hatching grounds its Argonians need. Its villages, logging camps and quarries along Cape Percar work timber and stone under licence, and Mir-Xal and Chasepoint carry the coastal trade. Whoever holds Bramman's river, the hidden channel from Topal Bay to the Blackrose lakes, holds the province's smuggling. Outsiders are welcome and are watched.
why: Soulrest is canon (Lore:Soulrest; story/lore/soulrest.md): Third Era capital, Topal Bay port, mines destroyed 3E 427, struggle for regional hegemony. Its 4E 201 state, mixed population and Bramman's river are argonia-4e201-state.md §Soulrest; no city Hist is an owner ruling. Seven of ten umber places lie on Cape Percar around the city. Acra-Tiin, Chasepoint, Mir-Xal, Naxan and Salaxul have no UESP page.
